title: Beyond the 956: Alfredo Echávarri, Pumas' 1962 promotion captain, dies at 86
excerpt: Alfredo Echávarri Olvera, the captain who led Pumas to promotion to Mexico's Primera División in 1962, has died at 86. He died Tuesday, November 10, 2026.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Alfredo Echávarri Olvera, the captain who led Pumas to promotion to Mexico's Primera División in 1962, has died at 86.

Echávarri died Tuesday, November 10, 2026, Club Universidad Nacional confirmed. No cause of death was disclosed.

Echávarri was a central defender and the captain of the Pumas side that won the Segunda División title in the 1961-62 season and sealed promotion to the top flight with a 5-1 win over Cataluña on January 9, 1962, at the Estadio Olímpico Universitario. He was studying architecture at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) while he played, spending four seasons in the Segunda División and then two more in the Primera División. Pumas has never been relegated since that promotion.

Known as “El Témpano” for the coolness with which he took penalties, Echávarri remained a revered figure among Pumas supporters long after his playing days. His daughter Andrea married Joaquín Beltrán, the Pumas captain of the club's 2004 bicampeonato team.

A memorial Mass for Echávarri was scheduled for Wednesday, November 11, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. at the Iglesia de la Santa Cruz del Pedregal in Mexico City.

Rest in Peace, Alfredo Echávarri.

Sources: Reforma; Infobae; TUDN; Claro Sports.
